summary: Oswald Richter was a scholar in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig under Karl Brugmann (~1893–1897), later serving at the Museum of Ethnology, Dresden (1898) and Berlin's Ethnological Museum (1904).

Otakar Klíma was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He earned his Ph.D. at Charles University (1927–1932) studying under Bedřich Hrozný, Vincenc Lesný, and Jan Rypka, and later directed the Near Eastern Section at the Czech Academy of Sciences (1953–1973).

Otakar Pertold worked in Indology and religious studies, earning his Ph.D. (~1903–1908) and habilitation (~1908–1912) at Charles University under teachers including Josef Zubatý and Wilhelm Geiger. He held docent and professorial posts at Charles University from 1919 to 1955.

Othmar Frank was an Indologist who studied Sanskrit under Alexander Hamilton at the University of Paris (~1814–1816). He held professorships at the University of Bamberg (~1802–1803), the University of Würzburg (1821), and the University of Munich (1826).
Otoya Tanaka was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1927–1930). He later served as a professor at Chuo University (~1960–1974).

Otto Albert Paul specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Wilhelm Geiger, earned his Ph.D. (1924–1927) and habilitated (-1938) at the University of Munich, and became director of the Institut zur Erforschung der Judenfrage in 1941.

Otto Benndorf was a historian and archaeologist who studied under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker at Bonn and Göttingen. He held posts at Zurich, Munich, Charles University, and Vienna, and directed the Austrian Archaeological Institute (1898–1907).
Otto Blau studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1848) and the University of Leipzig (~1848–1851), where he studied under August Friedrich Pott.

Otto Donner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Helsinki (M.A., Ph.D.) and under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Helsinki, including Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology (1875–1905).

Otto E. Neugebauer was a historian of mathematics and archaeology who earned his Ph.D. at Göttingen (~1924–1926). He held posts at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University (1939–1969), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1945; 1969–1990).

Otto Fischer worked in Sinology, Japanology, and art history/archaeology, habilitating at the University of Göttingen (~1910–1912). He directed the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920) and Kunstmuseum Basel (1927), and was professor of art history at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

Otto Franke was a scholar of Sinology and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held chairs at the Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut/University of Hamburg (1909–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1923–1931).

Otto Fredrik Tullberg was an Indologist and linguist who earned his master's at Uppsala University (1822–1830) and studied under scholars including Franz Bopp and Eugène Burnouf. In 1843, he was appointed Professor of Oriental Languages at Uppsala University.
Otto Grohma was a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1963–1971), where he subsequently served as an assistant beginning in 1972.

Otto Heinrich Wilhelm Keller was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. under Christian Bartholomae at the University of Giessen (1897–1904) and served as director at Gymnasium Michelstadt (1918) and Wolfgang-Ernst-Gymnasium (1925–1935).

Otto Hoffmann was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Göttingen under August Fick (1883–1888). He held professorships in Indo-European linguistics at the University of Königsberg (1896), University of Breslau (1907–1909), and University of Münster (1909–1935).

Otto Huth was a scholar of religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (1925–1932). He served as a Privatdozent at Strasbourg (1941–1944) and as a Privatdozent and later Professor at the University of Tübingen (1939; 1942–1971).

Otto Höfler was a scholar of linguistics and religion who earned his PhD and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He held professorships at Kiel (1935), Munich (1938–1945; 1954), and Vienna (1957–1971).

Otto Jahn was an archaeologist and linguist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin. He held academic posts at Kiel (~1839–1842), Greifswald (~1842–1847), Leipzig (~1847–1851), and the University of Bonn (~1855–1869).

Otto K. Schwarz specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a master's at the Financial University (2006–2011) and a PhD at the Russian Christian Academy for the Humanities (2021–2025), joining the Higher School of Economics faculty in 2026.
